title: Adaptive tenant shaper + kernel hinting for embedding p99 suppression
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Several high-traffic tenants experience long tail latency on the embeddings endpoint during bursty periods and when reranking jobs spike. Root causes from prior profiling point to: uneven microbatch formation (tenant mixing creates small residual batches), suboptimal kernel selection for short vs long sequence paths, and interference from off-path reranking requests that temporarily starve embedding queues. Goal: design and ship an adaptive per-tenant microbatch shaper plus kernel hinting mechanism that reduces embed p99 latency across tenants by at least 30% while maintaining embedding quality for reranking workflows.
acceptance_criteria: Aggregate embedding endpoint p99 reduced by >=30% under synthetic 3x load compared to baseline for targeted tenants
Per-customer p99 for top 5 tenants reduced to <300ms on small models and <450ms on medium models in our CI perf harness
No more than 1% regression in embedding cosine similarity on the reranking evaluation set (rerank-eval-v2) when using adaptive quant/route fallbacks
Feature gated and rolloutable by tenant with a canary path and metrics exposed in Console (per-tenant p50/p95/p99, batch size distribution, kernel hints applied)
Automated rollback if error rate or quality regression thresholds are exceeded during rollout
steps_taken: Completed packetized profiler run across 4 dedicated pools (pool-a..d) and captured kernel timeline traces (2026-02-26). Findings: ~62% of p99 cases show small microbatches (<4) followed by a single large microbatch that blocks completion and causes tail amplification.

Implemented 'tenant slab shaper' prototype in the microbatcher: assigns short-lived shaping tokens to tenants that preserve headroom for forming 6-8 sized microbatches. Prototype PR: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/15892 (merged to canary).

Added kernel hint metadata to the dispatch layer: per-request hint flags (PREFER_FUSED_ATTENTION, FORCE_INT8_FASTPATH) that the kernel selector can use without changing model artifacts. Patch: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/16111 (open).

Ran CI perf harness 'embed-load-fuzz' with fixed replay of production traces from 2026-02-20. Results: baseline p99 420ms -> shaper-only p99 270ms. With kernel hinting enabled top-line p99 230ms. Quality checks on rerank-eval-v2 showed 0.7% mean cosine change.
benchmarks: Synthetic 200 QPS burst test (small model, sequence 64): baseline p50/p95/p99 = 34/120/420ms; shaper+kernels = 30/85/230ms
Synthetic 120 QPS steady (medium model, seq 128): baseline p99 = 750ms; shaper+kernels = 420ms
End-to-end reranking throughput (64-query batch): no significant throughput loss (<5%) when using adaptive shaper; average rerank score latency reduced by 12% due to fewer long waits for embeddings
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decision: prefer tenant-local shaping over global queue reshuffle to limit blast radius and allow per-tenant tuning (chosen 2026-03-05).
Tradeoff: kernel hinting increases code-path complexity and requires additional telemetry; accepted because kernel selector already had stable API for hints and rollout can be gated.
Quality vs latency: allow adaptive quantized fallbacks (int8) for tenants that opt-in; require continuous eval on rerank-eval-v2 and automatic rollbacks if similarity loss >1%.
risks: Incorrect shaping parameters could throttle aggressive tenants and reduce throughput — mitigated by canarying and conservative default thresholds.
Kernel hint mismatches may cause suboptimal GPU kernel selection on some hardware families; mitigation: add hardware compatibility whitelist and monitoring alert if p50 shifts >15%.
Telemetry gaps: need per-tenant batch histograms and kernel-hint counters to diagnose regressions; added dashboard tickets to ensure coverage.
next_steps: Finish runtime patch (PR #16111) and add unit tests for kernel hint decoding (by 2026-03-15).
Expose per-tenant shaping metrics in Console (dashboard template under console/dashboards/embeddings-shaper) and validate with staging tenants.
Run extended soak with production replay at 72-hour window to validate steady-state behavior and tail reappearance patterns (start 2026-03-16).
Coordinate with solutions engineering to enroll two high-volume customers into an opt-in canary and monitor rerank quality daily for 7 days.
